From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Bridgepoint Advisors <org-design@bridgepointadvisors.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed span adjustment & sensitive transition plan

Team —

I ran the draft recommendations with Bridgepoint and wanted to surface a concise proposal for the leadership thread and HR coordination. The high-level ask: reduce manager span in the Serving Runtime pod from 10 -> 6 for the next 3 quarters and consolidate two small specialist IC roles into a shared tooling squad. Rationale and headcount impact attached (20270401_reorg_rationale_v1.pdf).

Key constraints and requirements:
- This is sensitive: several impacted folks are mid-cycle on performance reviews. We need aligned messaging before any 1:1s.
- Target timeline: announce to managers week of Apr 12, 1:1s Apr 15–23, public comms Apr 26.
- HR action items: finalize transition roster, prepare severance/offer bundles if backfills are required, and draft manager talking points.

Immediate questions for you:
1) Aditya — does exec budget clear for two net FTEs for Q2-Q4 (we'd cover via reallocation)?
2) Mina/Neha — can you confirm a private communication cadence and whether employment counsel should review the roster before manager outreach?
3) Lauren — operational risks if we reduce span (critical on-call coverage and PR timelines)?

Please treat as confidential for now. Bridgepoint is looped to support comms and role design where needed. I've attached a sensitive roster spreadsheet for HR only (sensitive_transition_roster.xlsx).

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for the write-up and attachments. Operational items to flag:

- On-call: consolidating specialist roles into a tooling squad could create single points of failure for gpt-kernel runtime incidents unless we keep two tech leads with on-call overlap. Recommend retaining a 0.4 FTE tech lead allocation to tooling for incident response.

- PR cadence: current release cadence is tied to the two specialist owners; if we consolidate, we should add a fortnightly cross-team sync for the first 8 weeks post-change. I'll own that sync.

- Performance reviews: we need to pause calibration windows for directly impacted people until after manager 1:1s are complete to avoid biasing ratings.

Small edits to the manager talking points (attached inline) — see the callout about career-growth options for affected ICs.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Serving Runtime Operations

Team —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few HR-specific points and requests:

1) Confidentiality: HR will treat the roster as privileged. Please do not cross-post the spreadsheet outside this list. We will run the roster through Employment Counsel for any compliance flags; that will take 48–72 hours.

2) 1:1 guidance: we'll draft a manager script (tone + key phrases) and a Q&A doc for managers that covers: performance review neutrality, internal mobility options, severance/offer bundles, and reallocation timing. Expect draft manager materials by Mon Apr 5.

3) Counseling & support: recommend offering optional career coaching sessions for impacted ICs (external vendor). HR can coordinate but needs leadership approval for budget ~ $12k.

4) Roster note: I reviewed sensitive_transition_roster.xlsx and flagged three names with active review notes. We need Aditya to confirm PIP status for those before any outreach.
